title: tests.py fails its seconds ceiling on a darwin host that sprint workers share, though every test passes
goal: A full tests.py run on a darwin host that several sprint workers queue on exits 0 when all tests pass: the seconds ceiling (darwin 20) is measured on the suite's own run time, not on a wall time that the host's other sessions inflate; seen 2026-10-10 in BG-45zpw2go: 87 passed, 21 s, 32 s and 30 s against 20 s, with six other clones waiting on the host lock and a load average near 4.
notes: SP-lyfnpu37 (2026-10-10): with four headless workers on the host, full tests.py runs took 23-40 s against the 20 s darwin ceiling and exited 1 though every test passed (BG-a3zs7s2y, ST-gdcn5467, ST-agxrnaoo, BG-45zpw2go workers); alone the suite ran 19.1-19.9 s with 93-94 ids, so it sits at the ceiling even unloaded. SP-dqkf3i42 (2026-10-10): one or two workers at a time, the unloaded suite ran 19.3-20.1 s with 97 ids; TK-g67asvm5 pushed it to 20.33 s and had to cut its own test (git calls, a hook sleep from 3 s to 1 s) to land at 19.75-19.98 s, so every later test addition meets the ceiling first. SP-ciqk6gt6 close (2026-10-10): the review story's done was refused three times at 100 ids, all passing in 20.06 s, 20.10 s and 20.34 s against the 20 s darwin ceiling at load averages near 3 from other sessions, and passed at 19.87 s and on the fourth try once the load fell under 2. SP-qxcj7fgy (2026-10-10): every worker's full run passed 100 ids in 19.9-21 s and four exited 1 on the ceiling; the review's run took 21.14 s with the reviewer running and passed at done once the load fell near 1.5.
